title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation, Integration, Known Issues, and QBR Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
summary: A consolidated playbook for enterprise onboarding and ongoing support: covers onboarding checklist, integration guidance, escalation paths, known issues and workarounds, health check cadence, and QBR materials.
body:
Purpose

This playbook consolidates the processes, checklists, and operational playbooks used by the Customer Success and Support teams to onboard enterprise customers, integrate Redwood Inference into customer environments, handle escalations, document and mitigate known issues, and run health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for CSMs, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, and SREs supporting enterprise accounts.

Scope

Applies to all new enterprise customers, major integration projects, and production incidents that require cross-functional escalation. This document complements product runbooks, security/compliance guides, and the internal support process documented in Support Process (linked in related pages).

Table of Contents
1) Onboarding checklist (pre-sales -> go-live)
2) Integration guide (typical patterns + example configs)
3) Escalation playbook (severity levels, SLAs, contacts)
4) Known issues and workarounds (triage + reporting)
5) Health checks and QBR templates
6) Ownership, SLAs, and escalation contacts

1) Enterprise Onboarding Checklist (Pre-sales -> Go-live)

Intro: Use this checklist as the canonical sequence for enterprise onboarding. Assign an owner for each item in the "Owner" column and track progress in the customer onboarding project in Jira/Asana.

Pre-contract (Sales handoff)
- Review contract terms, SLAs, compliance requirements, and data residency constraints.
- Identify primary technical contacts, security contacts, and procurement timeline.

Week 0 (Kickoff)
1. Kickoff meeting (agenda: success criteria, timelines, integration/traffic expectations, security posture). Owner: CSM.
2. Environment scoping: hosted vs. dedicated vs. private. Capture region, expected QPS, burst patterns, and peak sequence length. Owner: Solutions Engineer.
3. Credentials & network: confirm API key provisioning, IP allowlists, VPN/VPC connectivity requirements. Owner: Customer IT + SE.

Week 1-2 (Configuration & Integration)
- Provide SDK quickstarts and sample prompts.
- Share model recommendations and cost/latency tradeoffs for expected workload.
- Integration smoke tests: generate tokens, embeddings, chat sessions; confirm telemetry and tracing forwarding. Owner: SE.

Week 3-4 (Validation & Load)
- Run performance validation harness (example suite included in Integration section).
- Run quality evaluations with customer prompt set (capture baseline metrics).
- Confirm logging, cost dashboards, and alerting thresholds are configured in Console. Owner: CSM + SE + SRE.

Go-live
- Canary rollout: route 5-10% traffic for 24-72 hours; verify SLOs (latency P95 < target, error rate < 0.5%).
- Full cutover once canary metrics stable and stakeholder sign-off.
- Post-go-live 7-day hypercare: daily standups for the first week. Owner: CSM + Oncall team.

Onboarding Deliverables (examples)
- Onboarding runbook (customer-specific).
- Integration checklist completed in Jira.
- Baseline performance & quality report.
- Shared escalation contacts and SLA expectations.

2) Integration Guide (patterns and example configs)

Common Integration Patterns
- Direct API (recommended for hosted): quick start, minimal infra.
- Proxying through internal API gateway: for teams that want centralized auth/logging.
- Dedicated/Private deployment: for customers requiring guaranteed capacity, VPC, or on-prem.

Sample HTTP request (hosted API)
- Ensure X-Request-ID, Customer-ID headers for traceability.
- Example curl snippet: 
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
       -H "X-Request-ID: <uuid>" 
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
       -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"Summarize sales call notes"}' 
       https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate

SDK Initialization (Node.js)
- Example: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, region: 'us-east-1' });
- Recommended timeouts: 10s for short prompts, 60s for long-generation jobs.

Observability requirements (minimum)
- Forward request traces to Console (trace id mapping).
- Send token-level cost telemetry to billing integration.
- Set up alerting: error-rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 min, latency P95 > expected SLO.

Performance validation suite (run with SE)
1. Latency microbenchmarks: 50/250/1024 token sequences.
2. Throughput soak: sustained QPS for 30 minutes at target burst.
3. Quality regression: run customer prompt set and compare against baseline metrics (BLEU/ROUGE or custom scoring).

3) Escalation Playbook

Severity levels and SLAs
- Sev 1 (P1): Production outage or major customer-impacting failure (system unavailable, or >50% of requests failing). Target response: 15 minutes, oncall escalation within 30 minutes.
- Sev 2 (P2): Significant degradation (latency or errors impacting >10% requests). Target response: 1 hour.
- Sev 3 (P3): Partial degradation or non-critical integration issues. Target response: 4 business hours.
- Sev 4 (P4): General question, feature request, or low-impact bug. Respond within 48 business hours.

Escalation Steps (numbered)
1. Triage in Support queue: triage engineer verifies logs, reproduces issue, captures request IDs.
2. If P1/P2, open a dedicated incident room (Slack #inc-<customer>-<id>), notify SRE and Runtime engineers, and create a live doc for status updates.
3. Execute runbook steps (see Runbook section).
4. If root cause unknown after 60 minutes for P1, escalate to Engineering Incident Lead and Product.
5. Post-incident: run RCA and share Incident Review doc within 72 hours.

Contacts and escalation matrix
- Support triage: support@redwood.com (primary)
- Oncall SRE: see Oncall rota (internal link)
- Runtime engineering: runtime-eng@redwood.com (for kernel/scheduling issues)
- Customer Success escalation: cs-esc@redwood.com

4) Known Issues and Workarounds (triage + reporting)

Documented known issues should live in the Known Issues tracker and be referenced in onboarding docs. Below are high-priority items commonly encountered during enterprise integrations.

| Issue | Symptoms | Temporary Workaround | Permanent Fix Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tokenization mismatch for legacy tokenizer | Off-by-one tokens, truncation of last token | Normalize to utf-8 NFKC and use the Redwood tokenizer shim | Serving Runtime team |
| Occasional KV cache invalidation causing latency spikes | P95 latency spikes for specific sessions | Temporarily disable session affinity or reduce KV cache TTL to 60s | Runtime engineering |
| VPC peering route flaps during high throughput tests | Dropped connections between customer VPC and Redwood Private control plane | Use dedicated private link or schedule tests with bandwidth reservation; retry with exponential backoff | Network & Private Deployments team |
| Model quantization regressions for long-form prompts | Quality drop on prompts >2k tokens | Route long-form requests to full-precision variant until quantization patch released | Model Ops / Applied ML |

Reporting and escalation for new issues
- If support finds a new production-impacting bug, tag the ticket with "severe" and follow Escalation Steps.
- Add a summary to the Known Issues tracker with reproducible steps, sample request IDs, and impact estimate.
- For customer-facing communications, coordinate messaging with CSM and Product.

5) Health Checks and QBR Materials

Health Check cadence (recommended)
- Weekly: automated health summary (errors, latency P95, token usage) sent to CSM + customer stakeholders.
- Monthly: operations review with SRE/Runtime to discuss anomalies and capacity planning.
- Quarterly (QBR): business review that covers cost, quality, latency trends, feature requests, and roadmap alignment.

QBR Template (sections to include)
- Executive summary: key wins, open risks, and 90-day objectives.
- Usage & spend: tokens by model, cost per 1k tokens, anomaly calls outs.
- Reliability & performance: SLO attainment, incidents since last QBR, mitigation steps.
- Quality & evaluation: prompt set performance, regressions, improvement plans.
- Roadmap & requests: product features, dedicated/private deployment milestones, and timeline.
- Action items & owners: prioritized list with owners and due dates.

Metrics (minimum)
- Requests per minute (avg and peak)
- Token consumption (monthly and per QPS)
- Cost per 1k tokens (derived from billing integration)
- Latency P50/P95/P99 by model and route
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) and broken-down root causes

6) Ownership, SLAs, and Playbook Maintenance

Roles and responsibilities
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): primary relationship, QBR owner, coordinates hypercare.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical integration owner, runs performance tests.
- Support Engineer: first-line triage and initial resolution.
- SRE/Runtime: performance, capacity, and incident response.
- Product/Model Ops: model quality regressions and feature requests.

Playbook updates
- Owner: Head of Customer Success (Ava Martinez).
- Review cadence: quarterly review and after any Sev1 incident.
- Amendment process: Proposed changes in pull request, reviewers include SE lead and SRE lead.

Appendix A: Quick runbook snippets
- Capture a failing request: curl -H "X-Request-ID:<uuid>" -v "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/requests/<request_id>/trace"
- Rotate API key: nav to Console -> Settings -> API Keys -> Create -> Revoke old key after testing.
- Temporarily increase capacity for Dedicated customers: submit capacity request to infra-ops@redwood.com with customer id and time window.
